label: copy-phase input r early in long (L=9) sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never during original or delimiter steps), and almost always when the fed-back input is r (86% of activation mass; y adds about 12%). It is concentrated in L=9 sequences (88% of mass) at recall_idx 2-3 (t=11-12), meaning r was original token 1 or 2 and is now being re-input. Within that context activations are strongest; similar r inputs at recall_idx 1, or in L=7-8, are weaker or inactive. A small cluster (about 5% of mass) fires on the last step of L=9 sequences. It never fires on first occurrences of a token. Precision is low: most copy-phase r inputs in L=9 at recall_idx 2-3 do not cross the threshold, and the false positives look the same on the surface. The predicate gets roughly 0.2 precision and 0.6 recall on dev (0.70 mass recall); adding y or L=8 raises recall to about 0.82 (0.89 mass) but drops precision to about 0.07.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=r (+6.57), recall_idx=3 & in_tok=y (+2.66), phase=2 & in_tok=y (+2.23), prev_tok=d (+2.06), phase=2 & out_tok=2 (+1.98), t=11 (+1.95). Lower it: orig8=- (-2.73), to_go=1 (-2.17), orig3=m (-2.08), orig0=r (-1.93).
